pages.text: "I hate you, Grandma!" Yuki slammed the room door and went out. Grandma had reminded Yuki three times about wearing boots into the room. One boot lay on its side on the porch.
"I'll be alone! I'll sleep in the shed!" Boots on, Yuki stomped across the yard. Brown dog Momo trotted behind.
The shed was dark, with cold wind blowing through. Yuki sat on a straw pile, face buried in the scarf. "Grandma only nags."
Outside grew darker. Yuki's fingertips were cold. Momo rested their chin on Yuki's knees and whined. The smell of the brazier drifted from the room.
Yuki stood with just one foot inside the room. Without a word, Grandma covered the brazier with ashes. Yuki only fiddled with the scarf's end.
Under the quilt, Yuki stretched their feet and touched something warm. Lifting it revealed a round stone wrapped in cloth. "Why is this here?"
"I warmed it in the brazier and put it there earlier," Grandma said, still turned away. Yuki hugged the stone, then jumped up into her lap. "Grandma's Arms Are Warmest! Warmer than the stone!"
"Even though I said I hated you..." Yuki's nose stung. Grandma patted their back. "I heard. Still, I put the stone in before it cooled."
The next evening, Yuki fixed the scarf knot and sat by the brazier. Grandma took out a stone. Yuki wrapped it in cloth. "One, wrap the warm stone! Two, put it at the foot of Grandma's quilt!"

Grandma slipped her feet under the quilt and held Yuki's hand tight. "Oh, so warm! Hurtful words last a moment, but Grandma's heart stays warm all night." Yuki snuggled into her side. "Grandma's Arms Are Warmest!"
